    6 - Basemaps, decoration and projections¶

    Furniture and framing: web-map basemap under the data, Natural-Earth features (land / rivers / lakes) and coastlines, labels / text annotation, a map projection with a graticule, and a Bokeh theme.

    The web-map layers render in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), so we reproject the vector data to 3857 first (to_crs(3857)).

    Setup and data - the German states and a global temperature field.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")  # deliberately silence all warnings to keep the rendered docs clean

import io
from pathlib import Path

import holoviews as hv
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Image

hv.extension("bokeh", "matplotlib")  # Bokeh = interactive (the default); matplotlib only for barbs / projection

# This notebook lives in docs/examples/interactive/guide/, so the bundled sample data at the repo-root
# examples/data/ is four levels up. The kernel's working directory is always the notebook's own folder
# (true for nbval, nbconvert and JupyterLab alike), so one clean relative path is all that is needed.
DATA = Path("../../../../examples/data")

from digitalearth.interactive import InteractiveMap
from pyramids.dataset import Dataset


def show(m, static=False):
    """Return the **live, interactive Bokeh map** - pan, zoom, hover, and the toolbar are all real.

    Run the notebook (Run All / Shift-Enter), or open it in a trusted viewer, to see the maps draw; a saved
    .ipynb only shows them once a kernel executes their JavaScript. A few layers have no Bokeh glyph
    (``projection``, ``streamlines``, wind ``barbs``) and are drawn by matplotlib; for those pass
    ``static=True`` (projected maps switch automatically) to embed a PNG instead.
    """
    if static or getattr(m, "_projection", None) is not None:
        fig = hv.render(m.render(), backend="matplotlib")
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close(fig)
        return Image(data=buf.getvalue())
    return m.render()

The kernel's working directory is always the notebook's own folder # (true for nbval, nbconvert and JupyterLab alike), so one clean relative path is all that is needed. DATA = Path("../../../../examples/data") from digitalearth.interactive import InteractiveMap from pyramids.dataset import Dataset def show(m, static=False): """Return the **live, interactive Bokeh map** - pan, zoom, hover, and the toolbar are all real. Run the notebook (Run All / Shift-Enter), or open it in a trusted viewer, to see the maps draw; a saved .ipynb only shows them once a kernel executes their JavaScript. A few layers have no Bokeh glyph (``projection``, ``streamlines``, wind ``barbs``) and are drawn by matplotlib; for those pass ``static=True`` (projected maps switch automatically) to embed a PNG instead. """ if static or getattr(m, "_projection", None) is not None: fig = hv.render(m.render(), backend="matplotlib") buf = io.BytesIO() fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight") plt.close(fig) return Image(data=buf.getvalue()) return m.render()

    import geopandas as gpd

adm1 = gpd.read_file(str(DATA / "germany_adm1.geojson")).to_crs(3857)
adm1_4326 = gpd.read_file(str(DATA / "germany_adm1.geojson"))
adm1_4326["area_km2"] = adm1_4326.to_crs(3035).area / 1e6
ncep = Dataset.read_file(str(DATA / "global" / "ncep_tavg_07.tif"))
print("states:", len(adm1))

    basemap - a web-map basemap¶

    basemap draws a slippy-map basemap under the data; list_tile_providers() lists the names.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    InteractiveMap().list_tile_providers()[:8]
    InteractiveMap().list_tile_providers()[:8]
    Out[3]:
    ['CartoDark',
 'CartoEco',
 'CartoLight',
 'CartoMidnight',
 'EsriAntarcticImagery',
 'EsriArcticImagery',
 'EsriArcticOceanBase',
 'EsriArcticOceanReference']
    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=3857, title="German states on a Carto basemap")
m.basemap("CartoLight").polygons(adm1, line_color="firebrick", fill_alpha=0.05)
show(m)
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=3857, title="German states on a Carto basemap") m.basemap("CartoLight").polygons(adm1, line_color="firebrick", fill_alpha=0.05) show(m)
    Out[4]:

    features - Natural-Earth reference layers¶

    features adds vector reference layers (land, rivers, lakes, borders) from Natural Earth.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=3857, title="states with land + rivers + lakes")
m.features(land=True, rivers=True, lakes=True).polygons(adm1, line_color="black", fill_alpha=0.0)
show(m)
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=3857, title="states with land + rivers + lakes") m.features(land=True, rivers=True, lakes=True).polygons(adm1, line_color="black", fill_alpha=0.0) show(m)
    Out[5]:

    coastlines - the Natural-Earth coastline¶

    coastlines overlays the Natural-Earth coastline - Germany's North Sea and Baltic coasts here.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=3857, title="German states with coastlines")
m.coastlines().polygons(adm1, line_color="navy", fill_alpha=0.05)
show(m)
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=3857, title="German states with coastlines") m.coastlines().polygons(adm1, line_color="navy", fill_alpha=0.05) show(m)
    Out[6]:

    labels and text¶

    labels draws one label per feature from a column; text places a single caption at a coordinate.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=4326, title="labelled states")
m.choropleth(adm1_4326, "area_km2", cmap="viridis").colorbar()
m.labels(adm1_4326.assign(geometry=adm1_4326.representative_point()), "shapeName", text_font_size="7pt")
m.text(10.4, 48.3, "Bavaria", text_font_size="11pt", text_color="white")
show(m)
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=4326, title="labelled states") m.choropleth(adm1_4326, "area_km2", cmap="viridis").colorbar() m.labels(adm1_4326.assign(geometry=adm1_4326.representative_point()), "shapeName", text_font_size="7pt") m.text(10.4, 48.3, "Bavaria", text_font_size="11pt", text_color="white") show(m)
    Out[7]:

    projection and graticule¶

    projection reprojects the whole map onto a cartographic projection ("Robinson", "Mollweide", ...) and graticule overlays lat/lon lines; these render via matplotlib, so show returns a static image.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=4326, title="July temperature on a Robinson projection")
m.field(ncep, cmap="RdBu_r").projection("Robinson").graticule()
show(m, static=True)
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=4326, title="July temperature on a Robinson projection") m.field(ncep, cmap="RdBu_r").projection("Robinson").graticule() show(m, static=True)
    Out[8]:

    theme - restyle the whole figure¶

    theme sets the Bokeh renderer theme for every layer; pass None to restore the default.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=4326, title="night_sky theme")
m.theme("night_sky").choropleth(adm1_4326, "area_km2", cmap="viridis").colorbar()
show(m)
    m = InteractiveMap(crs=4326, title="night_sky theme") m.theme("night_sky").choropleth(adm1_4326, "area_km2", cmap="viridis").colorbar() show(m)
